name: Guwamu
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

sources.citation: Holmer, Nils M. 1983. Linguistic survey of south-eastern Queensland. Pacific Linguistics D-54. Canberra: ANU. (Part II 2.11 pp.177-178; 4.1 pp.179-180; 8.5 pp.204-205)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL7091.Q4 H65 1983
sources.note: For the 'Gunggari group' languages he studied (Gunggari, Bidjara, Marganj, Gangulu, Wirri, Birri, Ngawun — not Guwamu): 'Word or syllable stress is not significant in any of the languages studied here.. the second initial syllable often carries mechanically more stress than the others'. Guwamu ('guamu') appears only as a language his Gunggari informant called 'almost the same' as her own (pp.179-180).

sources.citation: Wurm, S.A. 1972. Languages of Australia and Tasmania. The Hague: Mouton. (6.1.10 Stress, p.57; Guwamu at pp.63, 66 and research-history chapter)
sources.note: Read via openlibrary.org search-inside snippets of archive.org item languagesofaustr0000wurm (print-disabled). 6.1.10 is pan-Australian: 'Only in a few languages has phonemic stress been observed. In most languages, the predictable stress is on the first syllable of words, with a secondary stress on the third and/or the antipenultimate syllable in long words.' Guwamu is not named in the stress section (only in fieldwork history and morphosyntactic examples).

sources.citation: Austin, Peter K. 2026. Adding value to legacy linguistic fieldnotes: an Australian case study. SOAS Working Papers in Linguistics (submitted 2025), 25 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Gives the full inventory of Guwamu sources: Wurm 1955 fieldnotes (AIATSIS PMS 4336, 138 pp. retranscribed by Austin 1976), Sim 1959 MS, Tindale 1938, Breen unpublished, Austin 1980 and Austin & Wurm 1981 unpublished vocabularies, Skinner 1985 La Trobe MPrelim 'Guwamu phonology and morphology', Buchanan 2012 dictionary, Wafer & Lissarrague 2008:322-324; all analytic work 'remain[s] unpublished'.

sources.citation: Oates, Lynette F. 1988. The Muruwari language. Pacific Linguistics C-108. Canberra: ANU.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Stress section 2.6 concerns Muruwari only; Guwamu appears in territorial notes and the comparative wordlist (Appendix A). Silent on Guwamu stress.

sources.citation: Breen, J.G. 1981. Margany and Gunya. In R.M.W. Dixon & B.J. Blake (eds), Handbook of Australian Languages vol. 2, 274-393. Canberra: ANU Press. (section 2.4 Stress, pp. 295-296)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: For Margany and Gunya (sister South-Maric dialects, not Guwamu): 'Main stress is regularly on the first vowel of a word'; long non-initial vowels attract apparent stress; optional secondary on 3rd syllable of 4-syllable words; morpheme-initial secondaries in 5+ syllable words. Guwamu ('Koamu (Guwamu)') mentioned only p.278 re Tindale's term Ngaragari; no Guwamu statement.
